newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico says no set date for Pacto meeting.
newsitem.headline: Mexico says no set date for Pacto meeting.

text.p: The chief spokesman for the Mexican Finance Ministry said Wednesday that no firm date has been set for reaching a new economic pact among government, labor and business leaders.
"There still is nothing definite," Alejandro Valenzuela told a news conference.
Each year since 1987 the Alliance for Economic Recovery (ARE), informally known as the Pacto, has set economic goals for the coming year.

The Pacto customarily meets in November, although labor groups have pressured the government to move it up to October this year, while business leaders have resisted the labor campaign, saying it should take place in November.
Valenzuela said the government would bring to the Pacto meeting goals of at least four percent GDP growth for 1997 and lower inflation next year.
Government and private-sector estimates calculate the 1996 inflation rate at about 26 percent and GDP growth at about four percent.

"We are going to look for the minimum rate of growth that we consider satisfactory, which is at least five percent," Valenzuela said, repeating the previously stated long-term goal of President Ernesto Zedillo.
He did not specify a goal for reducing inflation, although in previous news conference Valenzuela said the government would like to cut the 1996 inflation rate in half.
